Chief Complaint
Follow-up for myelodysplastic syndrome.

HPI
The patient is a 79-year-old woman who presents today for a scheduled hematology follow-up regarding her diagnosis of myelodysplastic syndrome. She reports that she has been feeling generally stable since her last visit. She denies any new onset of severe fatigue, shortness of breath, or unusual bruising. She continues to experience mild lethargy on an occasional basis, which she attributes to her ongoing MDS. She reports that she has received her scheduled blood transfusions as planned and has tolerated the procedures well without any acute reactions or complications. She denies any significant pain or new functional limitations.

Review of Systems
The patient reports no chest pain, no shortness of breath, no palpitations, and no dizziness. She denies any recent changes in weight, appetite, or bowel habits. She denies any visual changes or headaches. She denies any joint pain or muscle aches.

Social History
The patient lives at home with her spouse. She is retired and enjoys gardening and walking in her neighborhood. She denies tobacco or alcohol use.

Family History
Her mother had hypertension. Her father had type 2 diabetes. Her siblings are all healthy.

Vitals
Temperature: 98.4 F
Blood Pressure: 128/78 mmHg
Heart Rate: 72 bpm
Respiratory Rate: 16 breaths/min
Oxygen Saturation: 98% on room air
Height: 5'4"
Weight: 145 lbs

Recent Labs
Hemoglobin: 8.4 g/dL
White Blood Cell Count: 2.1 x 10^9/L
Platelet Count: 65 x 10^9/L

Medication List
Epoetin alfa (weekly)
Multivitamin daily

Exam
The patient is alert and oriented to person, place, and time. She appears in no acute distress. Her skin is pale but dry and intact. Mucous membranes are moist. Heart sounds are regular with no murmurs. Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. Abdomen is soft, non-tender, and non-distended. Extremities show no new areas of ecchymosis or edema.

Assessment
The patient is a 79-year-old female with a stable presentation of myelodysplastic syndrome. Her laboratory results demonstrate persistent low blood counts, which are being managed with periodic transfusions and erythropoiesis-stimulating agents. She is currently tolerating her treatment regimen well.

Plan
Continue current management of myelodysplastic syndrome. The patient will continue her weekly injections and proceed with her next scheduled transfusion as coordinated by the clinical team. We will monitor her hemoglobin and platelet levels closely. Follow up in four weeks for a repeat CBC and clinical evaluation.

Electronically signed,
D. Kowalski, NP
May 14, 2026
